title: Unruptured ectopic pregnancy: methotrexate inhibits DNA synthesis (dihydrofolate reductase)
vignette: A 26-year-old woman comes to the emergency department for pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding over the past 2 days. Today, the pain has increased, but she has had no nausea, vomiting, or orthostasis. The patient was treated for chlamydia cervicitis 3 years ago. She takes no medications and has no known drug allergies. On pelvic examination, the uterus is small and mobile and there is left adnexal tenderness. Pelvic ultrasound reveals a complex, 2-cm left adnexal mass with a gestational sac and yolk sac; there is no intrauterine pregnancy or free fluid. The patient is counseled on recommended medical treatment. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of the agent of choice for this patient?

clues.text: treated for chlamydia cervicitis 3 years ago
clues.note: Prior sexually transmitted infection (chlamydia) with tubal scarring is a major risk factor for ectopic pregnancy.

clues.text: 2-cm left adnexal mass with a gestational sac and yolk sac; there is no intrauterine pregnancy or free fluid
clues.note: A gestational sac in the adnexa with NO intrauterine pregnancy and no free fluid = an UNRUPTURED ectopic pregnancy, treatable medically with methotrexate.

whatMatters: An early, UNRUPTURED ECTOPIC PREGNANCY is treated with METHOTREXATE, a folic acid antagonist that inhibits DIHYDROFOLATE REDUCTASE -> depletes tetrahydrofolate -> INHIBITS DNA SYNTHESIS, preferentially destroying rapidly proliferating cells (fetal/trophoblastic cells). Answer D.
strategy: Recognize the unruptured ectopic (adnexal gestational sac, no IUP, hemodynamically stable) and recall its medical agent = methotrexate. Its mechanism: inhibits dihydrofolate reductase -> blocks DNA synthesis in proliferating cells. Reject mechanisms of other agents: progesterone-receptor block/uterine contractions (mifepristone), decreased LH/endometrial thinning (progestins), prostaglandin-induced contractions (misoprostol), and local inflammation impairing implantation (copper IUD) - none are used for ectopic pregnancy.

options.text: Blocks progesterone receptors, resulting in uterine contractions
Decreases LH secretion, causing endometrial thinning
Inhibits DNA synthesis to destroy actively proliferating fetal cells
Produces local inflammation to impair implantation

eliminations.label: Blocks progesterone receptors - mifepristone
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a progesterone antagonist (mifepristone) causing decidual necrosis and uterine contractions for medical abortion. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: mifepristone is used for INTRAuterine pregnancy termination, not ectopic pregnancy. ✅ Correct if: medical abortion of an intrauterine pregnancy.

eliminations.label: Decreases LH / endometrial thinning - progestins
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: progestins (e.g., levonorgestrel) thinning endometrium and suppressing ovulation (contraception). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this is a contraceptive mechanism, not treatment of an established ectopic pregnancy. ✅ Correct if: progestin contraception.

eliminations.label: Prostaglandin-mediated contractions - misoprostol
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: misoprostol (prostaglandin E1 agonist) stimulating uterine contractions (labor induction/abortion). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not the treatment for a tubal ectopic pregnancy. ✅ Correct if: cervical ripening/medical abortion.

eliminations.label: Local inflammation impairing implantation - copper IUD
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: copper IUD creating a local inflammatory/spermicidal environment (contraception). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it prevents INTRAuterine implantation and does not treat an ectopic pregnancy. ✅ Correct if: copper IUD contraception.

reasoning: Adnexal gestational sac with no intrauterine pregnancy and stable patient = unruptured ectopic pregnancy
Medical treatment of choice is methotrexate
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase -> blocks DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing cells
-> inhibits DNA synthesis to destroy proliferating fetal/trophoblast cells; answer D
mechanism: ECTOPIC PREGNANCY occurs when the blastocyst implants OUTSIDE the uterine cavity, most often in the fallopian TUBE; risk factors include prior sexually transmitted infection/PID (tubal scarring), prior tubal surgery, and prior ectopic. An early, UNRUPTURED ectopic in a hemodynamically STABLE patient (with an acceptably low/plateauing beta-hCG and no contraindications) can be managed medically with METHOTREXATE. Methotrexate is a FOLIC ACID ANTAGONIST that competitively inhibits DIHYDROFOLATE REDUCTASE, blocking the regeneration of TETRAHYDROFOLATE needed for de novo purine and thymidylate (pyrimidine) synthesis; this INHIBITS DNA SYNTHESIS and preferentially destroys rapidly PROLIFERATING cells - here the fetal/TROPHOBLASTIC tissue - halting the pregnancy. (Ruptured ectopic or instability requires surgery.) The distractors are mechanisms of drugs used for INTRAuterine pregnancy termination or contraception (mifepristone, progestins, misoprostol, copper IUD), not ectopic pregnancy.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid OB/Pharm > ectopic pregnancy: tubal implantation; risk = PID/STI, tubal surgery, prior ectopic; unruptured/stable -> methotrexate (dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor -> blocks DNA synthesis in trophoblast); ruptured -> surgery.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Unruptured ectopic -> methotrexate = inhibits dihydrofolate reductase -> blocks DNA synthesis.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on ectopic pregnancy, methotrexate, dihydrofolate reductase, tetrahydrofolate, or trophoblast? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Mifepristone (progesterone block), progestins (LH/endometrium), misoprostol (prostaglandin), copper IUD (inflammation) are for abortion/contraception - not ectopic.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: unruptured ectopic pregnancy = methotrexate (folate antagonist, inhibits DNA synthesis in trophoblast); ruptured = surgery.

keywords.back: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase -> blocks DNA synthesis

Pharm > mifepristone, progestins, misoprostol, copper IUD.

memoryHook: Methotrexate starves fast-dividing trophoblast of folate (blocks dihydrofolate reductase -> no DNA) - the medical fix for an early, unruptured ectopic.
